answers.questionText: What are S3 Life Cycle Rules and what are the two types of actions?
answers.actualAnswerText: Life Cycle Rules automatically move objects between tiers or delete them. Transition Actions move from tier to tier (e.g., after 60 days, after 6 months to Glacier). Expiration Actions delete objects (e.g., delete logs after 365 days, delete old versions, clean up incomplete multi-part uploads after 2 weeks). Rules can be created for prefix or tags.

answers.questionText: What services can receive S3 Event Notifications and what is special about EventBridge?
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 events can be sent to SNS, SQS, Lambda, or EventBridge. EventBridge can send to 18 other services, allows advanced filtering (match metadata like object size, file name), and supports replay. You must create resource policies to allow S3 to write to these services.

answers.questionText: What data types do Data Warehouse and Data Lake support?
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Warehouse is for structured data. Data Lake supports structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data.

answers.questionText: What are the three V's of data properties?
answers.actualAnswerText: Volume (size/amount - GB, TB, PB), Velocity (how fast - batch, real-time, near real-time), and Variety (structured/unstructured, sources like API, stream, human input, electronic devices)

answers.questionText: What are the S3 performance limits per prefix?
answers.actualAnswerText: Up to 3500 requests/second for PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE (write) and 5500 requests/second for GET/HEAD (read). S3 performance is measured by prefix, not bucket. You can double throughput by using multiple prefixes. There is no limit to the number of prefixes per bucket.
